thread:
Shilpa: Heads-up — planning a cross-account key-drain sim next Wed 09:30 PT. Goal: validate we detect and contain an operator account trying to export a customer wrapping key via the KMS proxy -> HSM path. Need quick input: RBAC changes, audit evidence, and IR playbook notes.

Kevin: FYI oncall will be paged for any anomaly during the sim. Can you share the minimal RBAC delta you need? keep it scoped. :eyes:

Shilpa: Minimal delta proposal: temp grant `kms:ImportKeyMaterial` + proxy serviceaccount escalate to `kms:GenerateWrappedKey` for one test key. Grant for a single test-tenant only, TTL 1h. We'll revoke at end.

Maria: That policy looks fine but two notes: 1) require `condition` on `request.time < timestamp("...+1h")` and `resource.name` == test-key. 2) we need to enable Key Access Logs at DEBUG for the proxy and set retention to 90d for the sim run so compliance has raw evidence.

Tom: From Legal/compliance — SOC2 & EU-regulated customers will want chain-of-custody evidence: IAM change request, attestation that the key material was not exfiltrated (HSM audit trail), and signed run report. Also confirm we informed affected customers pre-sim if keys are customer-managed.

Kevin: Ops checklist for the sim: snapshot current IAM bindings, create ephemeral credential via `aws sts assume-role` style flow for the test operator, run the export attempt in a controlled network, capture: proxy logs, HSM audit logs, KMS audit events, process list on proxy host, and network pcap of the session.

Shilpa: Example audit log filters to save: `resource.type="cloud_kms_key" AND protoPayload.methodName:("GenerateWrappedKey" OR "ImportKeyMaterial")` and proxy logs with request/response headers (redact secrets). I'll paste a sample IAM snippet.

Shilpa: ```json
{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateWrappedKey"],
      "Resource": "projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/test/cryptoKeys/test-key",
      "Condition": {"DateLessThan": {"aws:CurrentTime": "2026-03-25T18:30:00Z"}}
    }
  ]
}
```

Maria: Also add `kms:RequestTag/testing-run = true` and log that tag in the proxy so we can filter sim vs real ops. For HSM, enable operator ID in the audit (require dual-operator flag if available).

Tom: Add two compliance controls: 1) pre-sim approval ticket in JIRA with sign-off from Security and Legal. 2) Post-sim signed assertion that no customer secrets were exported and a list of collected artifacts.

Kevin: IR + rollback: veto path = immediate revocation of the ephemeral role + rotation of any affected wrapping key (if any suspicion). We should have a canary key that we rotate instead of touching customer keys. Also record timeline in the incident channel and file a short post-run blameless report.

Shilpa: One open Q: for BYOK customers where they hold private material in their HSM, do we need to run this sim in their tenant? My thinking: run a tenant-scoped sim using a synthetic wrapping key we create for the customer (not the real BYOK), and ensure proxy layer enforces `isSynthetic=true` tag. Thoughts?

Tom: Correct approach: do NOT touch customer-owned private keys. Use synthetic test keys scoped to the tenant and documented in the approval ticket. For regulated customers require outreach and opt-out window.

Maria: I'll prepare a runbook fragment with exact log retention settings, sample queries, and the HSM audit fields to collect (operator-id, command, signature, firmware-version). Will post here by EOD.

Kevin: I'll wire oncall playbook: page SRE + SecEng on any HSM export events and include a link to the JIRA approval.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window Wed 09:00-10:30 PT. Pager escalation enabled for sim. Use `#incidents` for any real alerts.

Shilpa: Great — I'll create the JIRA approval, mark keys synthetic, and post the final RBAC snippet. Thanks all :pray:
summary: planning cross-account key-drain simulation: RBAC, logs, compliance, and IR
